podcast.title: Early Brian Wilson Style
podcast.body: In 1963, Brian Wilson was noted for creating "rather garrison surf rock records," a genre distinct from the "symphonic pop" he would develop later. "still making rather garrison surf rock records."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 116: "Where Did Our Love Go?" by The Supremes

podcast.title: Intentional Guitar Distortion
podcast.body: A defining characteristic of Surf Rock was the intentional distortion of electric guitars, achieved through heavy reverb and by physically modifying guitars and amplifiers in ways that voided warranties. This practice was necessary because dedicated guitar pedals and other outboard effects were not yet available. "What we had here was electric guitar, as with lots of reverb. And unlike just about everyone else, the guitars were intentionally distorted."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: West Coast Emergence
podcast.body: Surf Rock developed on the American West Coast, becoming a significant musical trend in certain circles within Southern California. It was largely pioneered by Dick Dale and the Deltones and initially began as an instrumental genre. "For example, on the American West Coast, something that became known as Surf Rock popped up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock
